section: Viceroys of India - Canning to Mountbatten: key measures, acts and events
subsections: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation
FIRST - first Viceroy, only Viceroy assassinated and assassin

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Durbar — Occasion

(a) 1877 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
(b) 1903 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
(c) 1911 — Coronation of King Edward VII
(d) 1877 — Coronation of King George V
o: 1877 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
1903 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
accepted.x: The 1877 Delhi Durbar, held during Lord Lytton's tenure, proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India, or Kaiser-i-Hind.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate the options with swapped monarchs.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Delhi Durbars:
1. The 1877 Durbar was held during the tenure of Lord Lytton.
2. The 1903 Durbar was associated with the coronation of King Edward VII.
3. The 1911 Durbar was the only Durbar attended by the reigning monarch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1877, 1903 and 1911 Durbars were respectively associated with Victoria, Edward VII and George V, and the 1911 Durbar was the only one attended by the monarch.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the Durbar–Viceroy–occasion sequence.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 1911 Delhi Durbar was held during the viceroyalty of
accepted.x: The 1911 Delhi Durbar was held during the tenure of Lord Hardinge II and was associated with the coronation of King George V.
accepted.tq: Use the viceroy–event association rather than relying only on the year.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was NOT announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911?

(a) Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
(b) Creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province
(c) Transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
(d) Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
o: Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
Creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province
Transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
accepted.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 was enacted during the tenure of Minto II and was not an announcement of the 1911 Durbar. The other three measures were announced on 12 December 1911.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to a different viceroy and event cluster.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Partition of Bengal
B. Delhi Durbar associated with the coronation of Edward VII
C. Delhi Durbar associated with the coronation of George V
D. Annulment of the Partition of Bengal

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1903 Durbar, 1905 Partition of Bengal, 1911 Durbar, and the 1911 annulment of the Partition of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1905 event between the two Durbars.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Delhi Conspiracy Case of 1912 was associated with an attempt to assassinate
o: Lord Lytton during the 1877 Delhi Durbar
Lord Curzon during the 1905 Partition announcement
Lord Mayo during his tour of the Andamans
Lord Hardinge II during the state-entry procession into Delhi
accepted.x: In 1912, Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal attempted to assassinate Lord Hardinge II during his state-entry procession into Delhi.
accepted.tq: Match the conspiracy with its target, year and setting.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The anti-Partition movement which contributed to the revocation of the Partition of Bengal was known as the
accepted.x: The anti-partition Vande Mataram movement contributed to the revocation of the Partition of Bengal, which was announced through King George V in 1911.
accepted.tq: Separate similarly placed movements by linking each one to its specific viceroy-era context.
accepted.sec: Capital shift to Delhi, Delhi Durbars, summer capital, Partition of Bengal, Bihar reorganisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with Lord Canning?

1. Passage of the Indian Councils Act, 1861
2. Introduction of the portfolio system
3. Establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
4. Passage of the Indian Penal Code

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four measures are associated with Lord Canning's tenure. His period also witnessed the Revolt of 1857 and the introduction of income tax.
accepted.tq: Group the measures belonging to one viceroy and reject no unsupported item.

accepted.s: The Wahabi movement in the viceroyalty list is associated with
accepted.x: The Wahabi movement is listed among the important events of Lord Elgin I's tenure from 1862 to 1863.
accepted.tq: Use the short tenure of Elgin I as a direct chronological anchor.

accepted.s:
Which of the following was NOT associated with Lord John Lawrence?

(a) Establishment of the Indian Forest Department
(b) Telegraph link with Europe
(c) Development of canals and state-managed railways
(d) Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
o: Development of canals and state-managed railways
Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
Establishment of the Indian Forest Department
accepted.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 was associated with Minto II. The other three measures belong to the tenure of John Lawrence.
accepted.tq: Identify the measure separated from the surrounding viceroy-specific cluster.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

(a) Lord Mayo — Financial decentralisation
(b) Lord Northbrook — Abolition of income tax
(c) Lord Lytton — Vernacular Press Act
(d) Lord Ripon — Second Factory Act
o: Lord Northbrook — Abolition of income tax
accepted.x: The Second Factory Act was passed during the tenure of Lord Lansdowne in 1891. Financial decentralisation, abolition of income tax and the Vernacular Press Act were associated respectively with Mayo, Northbrook and Lytton.
accepted.tq: Look for the swapped viceroy in a set of otherwise correctly matched measures.

accepted.s: The term 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government' is associated with the
o: Financial decentralisation resolution of Lord Mayo
Local Self-Government Resolution of Lord Ripon
Indian Councils Act of Lord Lansdowne
accepted.x: Lord Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution of 1882 is described as the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government. Ripon is consequently called the Father of Local Self-Government.
accepted.tq: Connect the famous title with the exact resolution and viceroy.

accepted.s: The Third Burma War and the foundation of the Indian National Congress occurred during the tenure of
accepted.x: Both the Third Burma War of 1885 and the foundation of the Indian National Congress in 1885 occurred during Lord Dufferin's tenure.
accepted.tq: Use two contemporary events to identify the common viceroy.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

(a) Lansdowne — Durand Commission
(b) Elgin II — Indian Councils Act, 1892
(c) Curzon — Second Factory Act, 1891
(d) Minto II — Lyall Commission
accepted.x: The Durand Commission was appointed during Lord Lansdowne's tenure in 1893. The Indian Councils Act, 1892 belonged to Lansdowne, the Lyall Commission to Elgin II, and the Second Factory Act to Lansdowne.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive commission and then eliminate the shifted viceroy pairs.

accepted.s: The killing of Rand and Ayerst by the Chapekar brothers took place during the tenure of
accepted.x: Rand and Ayerst were killed by the Chapekar brothers in 1897 during the tenure of Lord Elgin II.
accepted.tq: Associate the named perpetrators with the correct viceroy and year.

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures was undertaken during Lord Curzon's tenure?

1. Police Commission under Andrew Frazer
2. Indian Universities Act, 1904
3. Establishment of the Department of Commerce and Industry
4. Partition of Bengal

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four measures are associated with Lord Curzon. His tenure also included the Coinage and Paper Currency Act, 1899, creation of the North-West Frontier Province and reorganisation of the ASI.
accepted.tq: Recognise the Curzon cluster and check every numbered measure.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

(a) Chelmsford — Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh tragedy
(b) Irwin — Quit India Movement
(c) Linlithgow — Gandhi-Irwin Pact
(d) Wavell — August Offer
o: Chelmsford — Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh tragedy
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy occurred during Lord Chelmsford's tenure. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact belonged to Irwin, the August Offer to Linlithgow, and Quit India to Linlithgow's tenure, not Wavell's.
accepted.tq: Catch the swapped viceroy–event pair, a common historical trap.

accepted.s:
The correct chronological order of the following events is:
A. Rowlatt Act
B. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
C. August Offer
D. Wavell Plan and Simla Conference

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The events occurred in 1919, 1931, 1940 and 1945 respectively. Hence the correct sequence is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their known years before comparing the middle positions.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Wavell Plan and Simla Conference is correct?

(a) They were held in 1945 and failed on Jinnah's stand.
(b) They were held in 1940 and resulted in the August Offer.
(c) They were held in 1946 and directly formed the Interim Government under Mountbatten.
(d) They were held in 1931 and resulted in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
o: They were held in 1945 and failed on Jinnah's stand.
They were held in 1940 and resulted in the August Offer.
They were held in 1946 and directly formed the Interim Government under Mountbatten.
They were held in 1931 and resulted in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
accepted.x: The Wavell Plan and Simla Conference were held in 1945 and failed largely because of disagreement over Jinnah's position.
accepted.tq: Use the year and immediate outcome together to reject nearby events.

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 consisted of
o: Cripps, A. V. Alexander and Pethick-Lawrence
Pethick-Lawrence, Irwin and A. V. Alexander
accepted.x: The Cabinet Mission consisted of Stafford Cripps, A. V. Alexander and Pethick-Lawrence.
accepted.tq: Test the exact membership of a named mission rather than its broad purpose.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

(a) Wavell — The Viceroy's Journal
(b) Hardinge II — My Indian Years
(c) Irwin — Fullness of Days
(d) Mountbatten — The Viceroy's Journal
accepted.x: The Viceroy's Journal was written by Wavell. Hardinge II wrote My Indian Years, while Irwin, as Lord Halifax, wrote Fullness of Days.
accepted.tq: Identify the memoir title attached to the wrong author.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the Indian Independence Act, 1947?

(a) It created the office of Viceroy and strengthened the Secretary of State's authority.
(b) It abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State.
(c) It transferred the capital from Delhi to Calcutta.
(d) It introduced the portfolio system in the provinces.
o: It created the office of Viceroy and strengthened the Secretary of State's authority.
It transferred the capital from Delhi to Calcutta.
It introduced the portfolio system in the provinces.
It abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State.
accepted.x: The Indian Independence Act, passed on 18 July 1947, abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State.
accepted.tq: Focus on the legal effect of the Act and reject measures belonging to earlier periods.

accepted.s: Lord Mountbatten replaced Lord Wavell as Viceroy after
o: the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 alone
the announcement made by Attlee on 20 February 1947
the announcement of the Partition of Bengal in 1905
the passage of the Government of India Act, 1919
accepted.x: Mountbatten replaced Wavell following Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date as the discriminator among major constitutional milestones.

accepted.s: Who founded the Archaeological Survey of India?
accepted.x: Alexander Cunningham was the founder of the Archaeological Survey of India, which was set up in 1861 under Lord Canning.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founder from the later Director-General and reorganiser.

accepted.s: The motto of the Archaeological Survey of India is
accepted.x: The motto of the Archaeological Survey of India is 'Pratnakirti Apavarini'.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official expression rather than a familiar national motto.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two early censuses of British India?

(a) The first census was synchronous in 1872 and the first non-synchronous census was in 1881.
(b) The first census was non-synchronous in 1872, while the first synchronous census was held in 1881.
(c) Both the first census and the first synchronous census were held in 1872.
(d) The first census was synchronous in 1881, while the first non-synchronous census was held in 1901.
o: The first census was synchronous in 1881, while the first non-synchronous census was held in 1901.
The first census was synchronous in 1872 and the first non-synchronous census was in 1881.
The first census was non-synchronous in 1872, while the first synchronous census was held in 1881.
Both the first census and the first synchronous census were held in 1872.
accepted.x: The census conducted under Mayo in 1872 was the first, but it was non-synchronous. The first synchronous census was held in 1881 during Lord Ripon's tenure.
accepted.tq: Separate the first census from the first synchronous census instead of treating them as identical.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

(a) Lord Mayo — First census, 1872
(b) Lord Ripon — First census, 1872
(c) Lord Canning — First synchronous census, 1881
(d) Lord Curzon — First census, 1872
accepted.x: The first census was conducted in 1872 during Lord Mayo's tenure. The first synchronous census was later conducted in 1881 during Lord Ripon's tenure.
accepted.tq: Match the census milestone with the viceroy, while distinguishing first from first synchronous.

accepted.s: Who was the only Viceroy of India to be murdered while in office?
accepted.x: Lord Mayo was the only Viceroy murdered in office. He was killed in 1872 in the Andamans by the convict Sher Ali Afridi.
accepted.tq: Use the uniqueness clue and verify it with the place, year and assassin.
accepted.sec: FIRST - first Viceroy, only Viceroy assassinated and assassin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lord Mayo was assassinated by Sher Ali Afridi in
o: Calcutta during the Partition of Bengal
accepted.x: Sher Ali Afridi, a convict, murdered Lord Mayo in the Andamans in 1872 while Mayo was on tour.
accepted.tq: Combine the assassin, location and year to avoid confusing two separate assassination conspiracies.
